name: Author instrumented components (analytics events by construction)
desc: Declare every interactive component's analytics events as DATA on the node, the same way you author its behavior/motion — so any app composed from these components is instrumented by construction, not bolted on later.
body:
Author every INTERACTIVE component with an `analytics` events manifest — the per-node instrumentation CONTRACT, the sibling of the behavior/motion a component already carries (#3810, epic #3809). The point: analytics is DATA on the component, so any app composed from these components captures usage BY CONSTRUCTION — a complete, uniform taxonomy, not hand-sprinkled tracking.
1. If a component is interactive — it exposes an action/event prop the user can trigger (`onClick`, `onChange`, `onSelect`, …) — it MUST declare the events it emits. `bsc ui doctor` flags an interactive component with no manifest as `no-analytics`.
2. Declare events as DATA, never code. Each event is `{ event, when?, props? }`: `event` is a stable snake/kebab name (`click`, `item_selected`, `filter_changed`), `when` is an optional human note on the trigger, `props` are the payload fields (name + type). A Button declares `click{label}`; a CollectionPage declares `item_selected` / `filter_changed`; a form field declares `changed`.
3. Keep the taxonomy stable + meaningful: name events for the USER ACTION (`item_selected`), not the DOM (`div_clicked`). Reuse the same event name across similar components so the composed app's analytics is consistent.
4. Do NOT write emit code. The component only DECLARES its events; a shipped, audited runtime does the emitting (epic #3809, slice 2). This is the code-vs-data invariant (#3283): the LLM authors data, the trusted runtime executes.
5. Payload minimalism + privacy: declare only the fields the event needs to be useful. Never put PII / secrets / raw user content in an event payload — that's an analytics data-collection change and rides the same privacy discipline as `author-compliant-components`.
6. Display-only / layout components (no action prop) don't need a manifest — instrument what the user ACTS on, not every wrapper.
When authoring or editing an interactive component, add its `analytics` manifest in the same pass, and run `bsc ui doctor` to confirm no `no-analytics` finding remains.
